title: Toledo — Equation Library of the Human–AI Readout Programme
description: The permanent, coded registry of every equation in the Human–AI Readout Programme together with its Coq (Th_coqc) formalisation. Th_coqc certifies that a lemma is closed under a stated finite model's global context — an internal-consistency check, never an empirical or physical truth claim. v1.6 registers 1,267 entries (610 root rows). Two additions: (1) a root registry extension (R2) bringing in `information-discrete-math` (IDM) as 18 Layer-0 roots under IDM's own verbatim identifiers (`delta_R`, `RD1`–`RD9`, `D`, `Z`, `Q`, `R`, `L_R`, `Keystone`, the accumulation/search primitives `A2`/`A3`), with 274 readings mapped one-per-identifier onto the already-verified 274/274-closed IDM Coq mirror (`coq_status: mapped_not_wrapped`) and a connection to the Genesis root only where the source text itself states one (3 quoted links; every other new root's `relations_note` records an honest non-finding rather than an invented parent); (2) Master Equation River v1.6 (10.5281/zenodo.22644712) registrations — 24 equations (21 existing occurrences plus 3 new codes). Also ships a Resistance Ladder (R0–R6 rungs, each `{held, evidence}` — never a collapsed score) and Reproduction Ledger per entry, computed at build time from `coq_status` plus cited reproduction/review evidence: three worked cards are cited honestly regardless of outcome (a gauge-algebra dimension check that PASSED; a Higgs-mass prediction from an existing Genesis equation that FAILED against the published PDG value, disclosed rather than softened; and an IDM number-ladder approximant check against an independent arbitrary-precision oracle that PASSED to the declared tolerance) — R5 (independent reviewer) requires a review record from another agent at independence class I2 or higher, and none exists yet for any entry. Adds a 20th MCP tool, `toledo_lint` (15 rules over an entry's own shape; it warns, it never blocks a build), and a public-facing ecosystem map page describing how Toledo relates to the other repositories in the same programme. Ships a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server and command-line client (20 tools over stdio, a SQLite/FTS5 search index, and a static read API published on GitHub Pages) that lets an AI agent look an equation up before using it, plus a human-readable documentation site on the same GitHub Pages deployment. Each entry carries an honest coq_status (closed, definition, wrapped_related, mapped_not_wrapped, axioms, open_prop, or not_formalisable). Scope: equations and Th_coqc only; papers, books and prose live in their own records and cite Toledo codes.
